book.title: Transformation: What Stays the Same When Everything Changes

reading.arc: The sequence takes the cube that stood still in Melencolia's court and lets it change: Trans_Pre adds translation, rotation and scale one at a time to a pickup, each with a two-line excerpt (`lerp`, `rotate_y`, a size factor), then a wedge ramp to four finished pickups. Trans_Introduction turns each operation into a crossing the body depends on (a carrier, a swelling cube, a turning plank) and then slides the far bank so an unchanged operation stops connecting. Trans_Translation stretches displacement into seven rides through x, y, z and a diagonal with thirteen pickups, ending at two door handles whose permitted paths differ; Trans_Rotation gives the turn its own hall: centre-pivot rides, four tilted bands walked by two body widths, composition order on a workbench, swept volumes, a twisted tunnel and five carousel profiles. Trans_Scale enlarges a furnished room fourfold around a body that keeps its size and compares the grown 45-cm door with a fixed frame. Trans_Body reverses the input (approach turns slats, contact deletes cells, distance shrinks blocks) and Trans_Pit hands it to clocks, so the body must fit what the room does anyway, before an airlock composes all three operations into a passage that opens on approach. Throughout, the question is the sequence's truth: what each operation preserves in an object versus what it changes in the space a particular body can use.
holds: The pickup cube as the carried object: still in Trans_Pre, collected on the carriers of Trans_Translation, invoked by the airlock ('the same three operations we added to the pickup cube'), and picked up again by Array's first line.

The refrain object-invariant versus bodily clearance, restated at the close of every hall in a different form: 'Which description tells you what happened?', 'preserving a shape and preserving what someone can do there', 'Sameness depends on which part of the encounter you keep'.

One short code excerpt per work, with `lerp` and `delta` introduced in Trans_Pre and re-met in the carrier, the landing, the pusher, the grower and the airlock; `delta` is traced back to Point_One's counter.
The gap or door as the recurring device: three gaps, a pit, a basin, a 45-cm door, a slat wall, a trench, timed lanes, an airlock.
An explicit forward handover in the last paragraph of every hall ('The next hall asks…', 'What will fit then?', 'continues changing even when you stand still').
Paired fixed-camera figures ('the camera has not moved') from Trans_Translation onward, each showing two states of the museum work from one standpoint.

hall_notes.note: Four stations add one operation each to a pickup cube with a line of code apiece, then wedges lead up to four finished pickups. Brisk and clean, the lightest hall; the three side markers are the only thing it shows without naming.

Three gaps crossed by translation, scale and rotation, then MOVE THE BANK slides the landing so the plank's unchanged quarter-turn stops connecting. The best-argued hall: the excerpts serve the feet ('the collision box must grow too') and the bank experiment lands the sequence's truth, but it is the only hall after Trans_Pre without a figure.

Seven carrier rides through z, x, y, back and diagonally, thirteen pickups, then two door handles (rail-guided and free) whose traces differ. Reads well and the three-trace figure is served by the text; the closing torus points forward cleanly.

Five headed sections: centre-pivot rides with a level deck, four tilted bands walked by 0.44 m and 1.20 m capsules, composition order on the workbench, swept cylinder and cone with three push buttons, then the tunnel and carousels. The densest and longest hall by 280 words; strong sentences, but the body comparison arrives without a location and the carousel has no heading.

A furnished room, a 45-cm door, a bottle: the room grows fourfold in one cut, the body lands on the top plate, descends, and walks through the enlarged door and then a fixed frame of the same size. Tight and vivid; the sequence's clearest single image, and the code claims (FACTOR, landings, 0.08 clearance, 1.8 x 2.4) all match.

A slat wall that opens where you stand, a lattice that deletes what you press into and keeps the cut for the next arrival, nine blocks that shrink with your distance. Reads as an argument about margins and residue ('made by measuring'); 'the caption' needs a noun.

Pushers, slabs and growers on timers, a section 'The constant' that states the sequence's thesis outright, and the airlock that composes all three operations as a welcome. A strong close; the 'middle route' sentence contradicts the map's fire cells, 'eastern' is a compass word, and two asides read as internal.

stumbles: Trans_Pit: 'The middle route lets you keep your distance' — the middle of the rotation room (x=6–8, rows 11–13) is nine `h:fire` cells, visibly burning in the museum (detection disarmed) and lethal in a plain grid run.
Trans_Pit: 'The eastern passage lets you walk around' — a compass direction a headset visitor cannot read; the floor caption says only 'CHOOSE A LANE / OR WALK AROUND'.
Trans_Introduction: 'changes from half a metre to three metres … The visible mesh begins as a one-metre cube' — two sizes for one starting state.
Trans_Rotation: 'Watch the cyan bodies begin' — no location for the study stand, and no word that the runs repeat on their own (the reader may wait for a cue).
Trans_Pit: 'A fraction marks its place along the journey' — reads as a visible mark; the block shows an arrow, the fraction is the script's `_t`.
Trans_Pit: 'No pickup count decides whether you may enter' — a negative nothing in the sequence set up.
Trans_Pre: 'The small markers beside the examples help you recognise each operation' — three side artifacts the text never introduces.
Trans_Body: 'The caption asks you to step clear' — the reader has to guess that this is the floor label 'SCALE / STEP CLEAR TO REGROW'.
Trans_Introduction and Trans_Translation hand forward by file ID ('Trans_Translation will give…', 'In Trans_Rotation, the turn…') where every other hall says 'the next hall'.
Trans_Translation: 'then move it outwards' after calling the same rail leg 'sideways'.

keep.quote: Contact, detection and this shared movement have to agree for the moving object to become transport. A beautiful motion can still leave someone behind.
The readout measures the seam. It cannot settle what your body can do with it.
The simulation supplies an opening and a duration. It does not know how long you need to understand what just carried you.
Your hand can propose a diagonal and leave a vertical line.
A shape can return without giving back the time it took, or undoing where it carried you.
There is a difference between preserving a shape and preserving what someone can do there.
What is kept is not what you intended. You meant to cross; the trench is the residue of the margin that let you.
The transformations did not become false when you entered the room. They became insufficient as descriptions of what the room allows.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Primitives_Melencolia ends by turning the court's stillness into the next question ('In transformation, you can watch from one place as objects move, turn and scale … ask what would survive such a change') and Trans_Pre opens on exactly that: 'In Melencolia, the pyramids stayed still while your viewpoint changed. Here, stay a moment and let an object change in front of you. What survives its movement?' The carried objects (cube, wedge, grid) are named in the second sentence, and Trans_Pre's remark that the first room's counter received `delta` without using it matches Point_One/final.md:28 ('Our counter ignores it'). Nothing to fix.
reading.handover_out: Clean. Trans_Pit closes on the airlock's three operations and 'What else could these three operations make possible?'; Array opens 'This is the cube we met at the beginning of Transformation. There, one body acquired movement, orientation and scale. Here it has company', and brings the operations back on the Molnár study ('These are the operations we brought from Transformation'). Array's 'beginning of Transformation' agrees with the book's use of 'chapter' for a sequence (Trans_Pit: 'the pickup cube at the beginning of the chapter'; Melencolia: 'You have spent a chapter assembling a vocabulary'). The only sentence near the seam a reader cannot place is the airlock's 'No pickup count decides whether you may enter' (a task below).
